12 /-!
13 # Real numbers from Cauchy sequences
14 
15 This file defines `ℝ` as the type of equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences of rational numbers.
16 This choice is motivated by how easy it is to prove that `ℝ` is a commutative ring, by simply
17 lifting everything to `ℚ`.
18 
19 The facts that the real numbers are an Archimedean floor ring,
20 and a conditionally complete linear order,
21 have been deferred to the file `Mathlib/Data/Real/Archimedean.lean`,
22 in order to keep the imports here simple.
23 
24 The fact that the real numbers are a (trivial) *-ring has similarly been deferred to
25 `Mathlib/Data/Real/Star.lean`.
26 -/
27 
28 @[expose] public section
29 
30

33 /-- The type `ℝ` of real numbers constructed as equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences of rational
34 numbers. -/
35 structure Real where ofCauchy ::
36   /-- The underlying Cauchy completion -/
37   cauchy : CauSeq.Completion.Cauchy (abs : ℚ → ℚ)

64 /-- The real numbers are isomorphic to the quotient of Cauchy sequences on the rationals. -/
65 def equivCauchy : ℝ ≃ CauSeq.Completion.Cauchy (abs : ℚ → ℚ) :=
66   ⟨Real.cauchy, Real.ofCauchy, fun ⟨_⟩ => rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩

126 theorem ofCauchy_zero : (⟨0⟩ : ℝ) = 0 :=
127   zero_def.symm
128 
129 theorem ofCauchy_one : (⟨1⟩ : ℝ) = 1 :=
130   one_def.symm
131 
132 theorem ofCauchy_add (a b) : (⟨a + b⟩ : ℝ) = ⟨a⟩ + ⟨b⟩ :=
133   (add_def _ _).symm
134 
135 theorem ofCauchy_neg (a) : (⟨-a⟩ : ℝ) = -⟨a⟩ :=
136   (neg_def _).symm
137 
138 theorem ofCauchy_sub (a b) : (⟨a - b⟩ : ℝ) = ⟨a⟩ - ⟨b⟩ := by
139   rw [sub_eq_add_neg, ofCauchy_add, ofCauchy_neg]
140   rfl
141 
142 theorem ofCauchy_mul (a b) : (⟨a * b⟩ : ℝ) = ⟨a⟩ * ⟨b⟩ :=
143   (mul_def _ _).symm
144 
145 theorem ofCauchy_inv {f} : (⟨f⁻¹⟩ : ℝ) = ⟨f⟩⁻¹ :=
146   show _ = inv' _ by rw [inv']
147 
148 theorem cauchy_zero : (0 : ℝ).cauchy = 0 :=
149   show zero.cauchy = 0 by rw [zero_def]
150 
151 theorem cauchy_one : (1 : ℝ).cauchy = 1 :=
152   show one.cauchy = 1 by rw [one_def]
153 
154 theorem cauchy_add : ∀ a b, (a + b : ℝ).cauchy = a.cauchy + b.cauchy
155   | ⟨a⟩, ⟨b⟩ => show (add _ _).cauchy = _ by rw [add_def]
156 
157 theorem cauchy_neg : ∀ a, (-a : ℝ).cauchy = -a.cauchy
158   | ⟨a⟩ => show (neg _).cauchy = _ by rw [neg_def]
159 
160 theorem cauchy_mul : ∀ a b, (a * b : ℝ).cauchy = a.cauchy * b.cauchy
161   | ⟨a⟩, ⟨b⟩ => show (mul _ _).cauchy = _ by rw [mul_def]
162 
163 theorem cauchy_sub : ∀ a b, (a - b : ℝ).cauchy = a.cauchy - b.cauchy
164   | ⟨a⟩, ⟨b⟩ => by
165     rw [sub_eq_add_neg, ← cauchy_neg, ← cauchy_add]
166     rfl
167 
168 theorem cauchy_inv : ∀ f, (f⁻¹ : ℝ).cauchy = f.cauchy⁻¹
169   | ⟨f⟩ => show (inv' _).cauchy = _ by rw [inv']

209 /-- `Real.equivCauchy` as a ring equivalence. -/
210 @[simps]
211 def ringEquivCauchy : ℝ ≃+* CauSeq.Completion.Cauchy (abs : ℚ → ℚ) :=
212   { equivCauchy with
213     toFun := cauchy
214     invFun := ofCauchy
215     map_add' := cauchy_add
216     map_mul' := cauchy_mul }

269 private irreducible_def lt : ℝ → ℝ → Prop
270   | ⟨x⟩, ⟨y⟩ =>
271     (Quotient.liftOn₂ x y (· < ·)) fun _ _ _ _ hf hg =>
272       propext <|
273         ⟨fun h => lt_of_eq_of_lt (Setoid.symm hf) (lt_of_lt_of_eq h hg), fun h =>
274           lt_of_eq_of_lt hf (lt_of_lt_of_eq h (Setoid.symm hg))⟩

525 /-- Show an underlying Cauchy sequence for real numbers.
526 
527 The representative chosen is the one passed in the VM to `Quot.mk`, so two Cauchy sequences
528 converging to the same number may be printed differently.
529 -/
530 unsafe instance : Repr ℝ where
531   reprPrec r p := Repr.addAppParen ("Real.ofCauchy " ++ repr r.cauchy) p
532 
533 theorem le_mk_of_forall_le {f : CauSeq ℚ abs} : (∃ i, ∀ j ≥ i, x ≤ f j) → x ≤ mk f := by
534   intro h
535   induction x using Real.ind_mk
536   apply le_of_not_gt
537   rw [mk_lt]
538   rintro ⟨K, K0, hK⟩
539   obtain ⟨i, H⟩ := exists_forall_ge_and h (exists_forall_ge_and hK (f.cauchy₃ <| half_pos K0))
540   apply not_lt_of_ge (H _ le_rfl).1
541   rw [← mk_const, mk_lt]
542   refine ⟨_, half_pos K0, i, fun j ij => ?_⟩
543   have := add_le_add (H _ ij).2.1 (le_of_lt (abs_lt.1 <| (H _ le_rfl).2.2 _ ij).1)
544   rwa [← sub_eq_add_neg, sub_self_div_two, sub_apply, sub_add_sub_cancel] at this
545 
546 theorem mk_le_of_forall_le {f : CauSeq ℚ abs} {x : ℝ} (h : ∃ i, ∀ j ≥ i, (f j : ℝ) ≤ x) :
547     mk f ≤ x := by
548   obtain ⟨i, H⟩ := h
549   rw [← neg_le_neg_iff, ← mk_neg]
550   exact le_mk_of_forall_le ⟨i, fun j ij => by simp [H _ ij]⟩
551 
552 theorem mk_near_of_forall_near {f : CauSeq ℚ abs} {x : ℝ} {ε : ℝ}
553     (H : ∃ i, ∀ j ≥ i, |(f j : ℝ) - x| ≤ ε) : |mk f - x| ≤ ε :=
554   abs_sub_le_iff.2
555     ⟨sub_le_iff_le_add'.2 <|
556         mk_le_of_forall_le <|
557           H.imp fun _ h j ij => sub_le_iff_le_add'.1 (abs_sub_le_iff.1 <| h j ij).1,
558       sub_le_comm.1 <|
559         le_mk_of_forall_le <| H.imp fun _ h j ij => sub_le_comm.1 (abs_sub_le_iff.1 <| h j ij).2⟩
560 
561 lemma mul_add_one_le_add_one_pow {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (b : ℕ) : a * b + 1 ≤ (a + 1) ^ b := by
562   rcases ha.eq_or_lt with rfl | ha'
563   · simp
564   clear ha
565   induction b generalizing a with
566   | zero => simp
567   | succ b hb =>
568     calc
569       a * ↑(b + 1) + 1 = (0 + 1) ^ b * a + (a * b + 1) := by
570         simp [mul_add, add_assoc, add_left_comm]
571       _ ≤ (a + 1) ^ b * a + (a + 1) ^ b := by
572         gcongr
573         · norm_num
574         · exact hb ha'
575       _ = (a + 1) ^ (b + 1) := by simp [pow_succ, mul_add]
576 
577 end Real

579 /-- A function `f : R → ℝ` is power-multiplicative if for all `r ∈ R` and all positive `n ∈ ℕ`,
580 `f (r ^ n) = (f r) ^ n`. -/
581 def IsPowMul {R : Type*} [Pow R ℕ] (f : R → ℝ) :=
582   ∀ (a : R) {n : ℕ}, 1 ≤ n → f (a ^ n) = f a ^ n
583 
584 lemma IsPowMul.map_one_le_one {R : Type*} [Monoid R] {f : R → ℝ} (hf : IsPowMul f) :
585     f 1 ≤ 1 := by
586   have hf1 : (f 1) ^ 2 = f 1 := by conv_rhs => rw [← one_pow 2, hf _ one_le_two]
587   rcases eq_zero_or_one_of_sq_eq_self hf1 with h | h <;> rw [h]
588   exact zero_le_one

590 /-- A ring homomorphism `f : α →+* β` is bounded with respect to the functions `nα : α → ℝ` and
591   `nβ : β → ℝ` if there exists a positive constant `C` such that for all `x` in `α`,
592   `nβ (f x) ≤ C * nα x`. -/
593 def RingHom.IsBoundedWrt {α : Type*} [Ring α] {β : Type*} [Ring β] (nα : α → ℝ) (nβ : β → ℝ)
594     (f : α →+* β) : Prop :=
595   ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x : α, nβ (f x) ≤ C * nα x
